name: Chalkboard
summary: Drawn live with pastel chalk on a slate-green board: side-of-the-chalk fills, cool hatched shadows, eraser wipes and line boil on twos.
description: The whole world is one big blackboard drawing. Every form is built like a real chalk drawing: the board is wiped clean behind it, a side-of-the-chalk fill of broken parallel dashes gives the colour (heavier in the light from the upper left), cool lavender hatching sits in the shadow, a warm stroke catches the light and a tip-of-the-chalk outline presses harder on the shadow side. The board's tooth punches clustered holes through everything. Figures are redrawn on a 12 fps clock (each actor holds a drawing for 2 or 3 ticks), are sketched onto the board in one sweeping stroke when they appear and are wiped off by a felt eraser in zig-zag passes when they go, leaving a dusty smear.
avoidFor: projects needing photographic depth or dramatic lighting

difficulty.why: The loose stroke forgives imprecision, but every new figure is posed in parametric poses (walk 8, idle 3, creatures 6), each pose baked in 2-3 redrawn variants, built with the fill-board / side-fill / cool-hatch / weighted-outline recipe, then grained and given a board halo; new ground regions need their own tileable stroke texture and a distance field for their border.

technique.resolution: Native resolution. Sprites are baked at K = clamp(round(screenH/360*4)/4, 2, 3.5) px per world unit; ground chunks at up to 2.5 px per unit (groundResMax 2.5, 256-unit chunks).
technique.summary: A small chalk toolkit (stroke, side fill, hatch, rub) draws every pose into an offscreen sprite; a 128x128 board-tooth mask is punched out with destination-out and a solid board-coloured halo is baked behind the figure, so actors read on the busy hatched ground. At run time only cached canvases are swapped on a 12 fps clock.
technique.linework: Tip-of-the-chalk strokes resampled every 1 unit with +-0.12 unit jitter, split into runs of 3-7 points, each run with its own width (x0.78-1.18) and alpha (x0.72-1.0); closed shapes overshoot 1-3 points; a second offset pass at 45% width and 40% alpha. Outlines get an extra pass (x0.75 width) where the edge faces the lower right, so the shadow side is pressed harder. Widths: main character body 0.95, head 1.2, small creature 0.95, large creature 1.5, props 1.0-1.2, details 0.35-0.6 units. Round caps and joins.
technique.shading: No gradients as light. Each form = board-colour occlusion fill, a faint flat rub (alpha 0.1-0.3), a side-of-the-chalk fill (broken dashes 1.1-4.6 units long at -0.42 rad, spacing 0.46, 28-40% gaps, a slow pressure wave, alpha falling off towards the lower right), cool hatching on an offset shadow ellipse (lavender #c2acec or violet #9680ce, spacing ~1.05, angle 0.82 rad) and a warm side-fill patch in the upper left (cream #f4e8ce or butter yellow #f9e58c).
technique.lighting: One light from the upper left for every figure, prop and the ground. Matte: the only 'glows' are faint orange chalk rubs (alpha 0.035-0.05, three rings r 8.8-12.5 units) around the main character's head and yellow rubs behind lanterns; eyes and mouths are solid butter-yellow chalk on board-coloured holes.
technique.texture: Board tooth: clustered pores from two octaves of periodic noise (dropouts in clumps with calm areas between), 5% single deep pores and 90 short drag streaks at -0.38 rad, punched out of every sprite at 0.3-0.9 strength. On the ground: baked smudge texture, macro brightness drift and old eraser wipes over half-erased drawings.

paletteRules: The board colour #25332d covers most of the screen; chalk never fills an area to full opacity except eyes, pupils and tiny details – the board always shows through the side fill.
Every chalk colour is a pastel; no saturated primaries, no black, no pure white (#eeeee5 is the brightest).
Shadows are cooler, not darker: lavender or violet hatching on top of the form colour; light is a warm cream or yellow stroke in the upper left.

Each region and each creature type owns one chalk colour: meadow = mint, forest = lavender, fields = orange/yellow, pond = light blue; small creature = lavender or pink shoulder, fast = white + blue, large = lavender with an orange core.
Holes inside sprites (eyes, mouths) are filled with the board colour, never with black.
Wood brown only appears on the frame and the eraser.

world.summary: An infinite blackboard map. Noise fields define forest, fields, pond and meadow; their signed distance draws crisp 0.5-unit white chalk borders and drives where texture is dense (along edges, in clusters) and where the board stays calm. Paths are dusty walked bands. Decals (eraser wipes over half-erased drawings, doodle groups, handwritten words, pebbles) cluster at features instead of being sprinkled.
layers: Board base #25332d + macro brightness drift (fbm /520, +-11) + a baked smudge texture

Regions: forest where a warped fbm (/760) < 0.455, fields where it is > 0.553, pond where a second fbm (/420) > 0.585, meadow elsewhere; borders = 0.5-unit white chalk lines from the signed distance (value / gradient), alpha 0.8 x grain
Region dust tint (3-5% of the region colour) plus a side-of-the-chalk band just inside each edge (5-15%) that fades over 5-7 units

Region chalk: forest lavender cross-hatch dense for the first 5-30 units inside the edge, then only in clusters; fields = Worley plots (82-unit cells), three orange/yellow furrow patterns, each plot with its own direction and offset, a third drawn as outline only, yellow 0.42-unit plot borders; pond = blue rub along the shore, three ripple lines parallel to it at 2.8 / 5.9 / 9.5 units, a darker damp middle; meadow grass only in clumps along borders, beside paths and in a few patches
Paths: 17-unit winding bands with a faint dust rub, broken edge lines 0.8 units inside and stipple dust in patches

Decals: a few big old eraser wipes per screen, each over a half-erased older doodle or word; doodles (star, moon, bat, spiral, heart, tic-tac-toe ...) in small groups; Rock Salt words; pebble groups along path edges

characters.summary: Doodle figures with designed silhouettes, posed parametrically and baked per pose: a main character with a big carved orange head, a curled stem, a long mint scarf and a tattered white cloak; small root-bulb creatures in two variants (round lavender-shouldered and tall pink-shouldered), a hooded wisp with a long streaming tail (two variants), and a hunched root giant with knuckle-dragging arms, a leaf crown and a lit carved core.
rules: Main character: ~18 units wide, ~31 tall, drawn facing right with feet at (0,0); head ellipse 7.8 x 6.7 with 6 lobes and deep-orange ribs, violet hatch on its lower right, stem with a curled tendril and a leaf as the signature; two-bone IK legs ending in lavender boots.

Small creature: bulb about 16 x 17 on stubby root legs (feet at 0, body centre 13.6 up), rootlet arms with three claws, a curly taproot tail, one heavy brow over yellow pupils and a toothy slit; variants differ in bulb proportion, shoulder colour and leaf count.

Fast creature: hooded head r 6.3 plus a tail that tapers over 13.5 units and carries a travelling wave; one reaching three-claw arm; variant 1 has a pointed hood and a frayed tail. Hollow board-coloured eyes and mouth.
Large creature: about 44 x 58 units, near arm cream, far arm lavender, nine-point carved core in orange and yellow; heavy stomp with 5.5% squash and a dust puff baked under the planted foot.
Every shape gets a board-colour fill first, so lines behind it disappear – that is how overlap works in chalk.
A solid board-coloured halo (0.6-1.1 units, 10 directions x 2 radii, alpha 0.6-0.9) is baked behind every figure; faint rubs do not cast it.
Far limbs are drawn in lavender, near limbs in white or cream – depth through temperature, not darkness.

props.summary: Props are doodles drawn with the same recipe, in 2-3 designed variants per kind, placed in composed clusters: a belt of trees inside forest edges with toadstools at their feet, reeds hugging the pond shore, stones and signposts beside paths, little graveyards of 2-4 stones, gourds in the field plots, fences along field edges.
rules: Round tree (mint crown), autumn tree (orange crown), pine (stacked tiers), bare tree (recursive branches, sometimes a bat), gravestones (round with 'RIP', cross, pointed), fence, scarecrow in a lavender coat, gourd groups, signpost, reeds, stones, toadstools, bush.
Outline 1.0-1.2 units, details 0.35-0.6; board halo 0.6-0.85 units; soft grained contact shadow per size class (tree 16 x 4, small 8 x 2.2, wide 18 x 2.6, tiny 5 x 1.5).

Swaying props (trees, reeds, bushes, scarecrow) own three drawings – leaning left, upright, leaning right by 0.01-0.05 rad about the foot – swapped on 6 fps ticks by a slow two-sine gust with a per-prop phase.
A tall prop (tree, pine, bare tree, scarecrow) that stands in front of the main character is drawn at 42% opacity, easing back to full 16-30 units to the side, so the main character is never hidden.
Placement uses 44-unit cells; nothing tall within 11 units of a path or 95 units of the start point.

effects.name: Appear: sketched in
effects.how: 0.45 s on twos: the construction sketch (tip lines only) is revealed by a clockwise sweep from 12 o'clock with a bright chalk-tip dot riding the edge; from 42% the coloured drawing fades in, then a small squash-and-stretch pop settles it.

effects.name: Disappear: eraser wipe
effects.how: 0.35 s: a 50 ms white recoil (1.13 x 0.89 squash + flash), then a felt eraser (wood top #b08058, grey felt) wipes the figure in 3 zig-zag bands (4 on the large creature); wiped parts remain as a 30% smeared haze; a tinted smear decal (16 dust streaks) stays on the board for 2.8 s.

effects.name: Impact
effects.how: Core: a hard white four-ray chalk tick (0.1 s, shrinking). Main: 6-8 radiating chalk strokes around a rubbed star that pop in at 0.55 -> 1.25 size and settle (0.26 s; yellow for orbiting hits, orange for dash hits). Debris: 2-4 crumbs in the creature's colours with gravity. Residue: a small dust puff (0.45 s).

effects.name: Burst
effects.how: Core tick, then a scalloped chalk poof (6-8 lobes, side fill inside a tip outline, two curls) in the creature's colour that bursts in with an overshoot and thins out over 0.42 s, 6-12 bouncing crumbs, 2-4 drifting dust motes and the smear on the board.

effects.name: Projectile: chalk seed
effects.how: Cream seed 6.6 x 3.8 with a white outline, behind it rows of short broken white dashes that grow in over the first 0.12 s; two redrawn variants, a slight spin wobble.

effects.name: Collectibles
effects.how: Small = light-blue gem, large = pink star with a yellow core; they float with hang time (1.6 units), pop out of the creature with an overshooting hop, and the large one gets a twinkle tick every ~1.8 s. Collecting = a white tick plus a rising yellow chalk star (three extra small stars for the large one).

effects.name: Orbiting lantern
effects.how: A carved orange lantern (3 redrawn variants) that swings against its direction of travel (follow-through), floats with hang time and drags a dusty chalk streak along the orbit tangent.

effects.name: Dash and celebration
effects.how: Dash: three fading chalk after-images, two speed strokes and white/mint dust behind the feet. Celebration: a rotating double chalk ring (yellow + orange with 12 ticks), a big tick, 8 stars flying out at 70 units/s and yellow dust.

atmosphere.summary: Matte, unlit chalk: no real light and no additive blending. Light is a direction (upper left) baked into every form, shadows are soft grained contact ellipses, a board-coloured halo clears space around each figure, and a baked wooden frame with vignette, chalk sticks and settled dust encloses the screen.
rules: Contact shadows: radial ellipses rgba(12,20,16,.62) -> .38 at 62% -> 0, grained at 0.5; main character 7 x 2.2, small creature 7.5 x 2.3, fast creature 4.8 x 1.4 (tightens when it dips), large 18 x 4.6; the shadow stretches 1.35 x 0.8 during the dash and fades during the eraser wipe.
Glows are faint chalk rubs, never light: orange rings at alpha 0.035-0.05 around the main character's head, yellow behind lanterns.
Board halo: the board colour around each sprite erases the busy ground texture locally, like wiping space before drawing a figure – the key readability device.
Edge vignette rgba(6,12,9,.5 -> .18 -> 0) over 10% of the height / 7% of the width.
Wooden frame (thickness max(8 px, 1.3% of H), bottom ledge 1.8x) with wood-grain strokes, chalk sticks and an eraser on the ledge, 700 chalk-dust specks above the ledge.
Colour grading: none; the board colour itself sets the mood.

ui.summary: The HUD is chalk on the board: wobbly white chalk outlines with uneven border radii, fills made of diagonal hatching stripes, Cabin Sketch values, Architects Daughter labels, Fredericka the Great titles underlined with an orange chalk stroke, cards tilted by up to 1.6 deg and pinned with coloured magnets, and one SVG noise mask that gives every HUD element the same board-tooth holes as the canvas art. A chalk clock dial hangs under the clock readout when the HUD is visible.

motion: Everything is redrawn on a 12 fps clock: each actor holds a drawing for 2 or 3 ticks (chosen by its seed) before switching to the next of its 2-3 redrawn variants, so a crowd never boils in lock-step.

Main character walk: 8 poses (contact, down, passing, up per step) at ~10 poses/s; the body drops 0.95 units on the down pose, the head follows one pose late, scarf and cloak hem lag behind; arms counter-swing.
Idle: three breathing poses played 0-1-2-1 at 0.45 s each, a blink every 3.4 s for 0.14 s, head roll and scarf drift; per-instance phase offset.

Dash: a crouch-and-lean-back anticipation drawing, the stretched dash drawing with the scarf streaming back, then a 120 ms landing crouch. Hurt: a recoil drawing (head thrown back, arms up, mouth open) for 150 ms with a white flash, then 0.75 s of blinking.

Creatures: 6-pose cycles driven by stride (small ~6 poses/s with squash at contact, large ~5 poses/s with a stomp), the fast creature flutters on a time-driven 6-pose loop and floats with hang time (smoothstep on a triangle wave), never a plain sine.
Hit: 140 ms squash (1.17 x 0.86), 0.2 rad lean away from the blow, a 1.4-unit shove and a white chalk flash copy; the large creature reacts at 55%.
Effects age on the 12 fps clock too (sizes step, positions stay smooth); floating numbers scrawl in with an overshoot (0.55 -> 1.15 -> 1) and are rubbed out over the last 0.22 s.
Ambient: swaying props swap lean drawings on 6 fps ticks; burst smears and ground wipes stay still.
do: Draw every form with the recipe: board fill, faint rub, side-of-the-chalk fill heavier in the light, cool hatching in the shadow, a warm stroke in the light, an outline pressed harder on the shadow side.
Keep one light direction (upper left) for figures, props and the ground.
Pose figures parametrically (feet, body drop, lean, lagging head and cloth) and bake each pose in 2-3 redrawn variants.
Hold drawings for 2-3 ticks of a 12 fps clock, with a per-actor offset.
Punch the board-tooth mask out of every baked sprite, word and HUD element; bake a solid board-coloured halo behind figures.
Cluster texture and props at features (edges, shores, paths) and leave large calm board areas.
Make appearance and destruction chalk-native: sketched in, wiped by an eraser, dust, crumbs and smears.
dont: Don't use smooth gradients as lighting, glows with 'lighter' blending, or hard drop shadows.
Don't use black outlines or pure white – chalk is #eeeee5 at most.
Don't fill shapes at full opacity – the board must show through the side fill.
Don't darken shadows with black or grey; hatch them in a cooler chalk.
Don't scatter grass or doodles evenly over the whole ground.
Don't regenerate strokes every frame or rotate sprites per frame – bake drawings once and swap them.
Don't animate with smooth tweens on every frame; hold poses on twos.
performance: Expensive at init, cheap per frame. At init: the board-tooth mask, five 512x512 tileable ground textures and the first variant of every pose, prop and particle. The remaining redrawn variants are baked in requestIdleCallback slices of 4-10 ms between frames, mirrored copies and prop lean drawings are made once on first use. Ground chunks are built by a generator inside the renderer's 5 ms per-frame budget: a 64x64 grid of noise fields and distances, a per-pixel composite (Worley noise only inside fields), putImageData in 96-row bands, then decals. Per frame: axis-aligned drawImage of cached canvases; only hits, spawns, deaths, orbiting lanterns and particles use a transform. Hot spots: the per-pixel ground loop and the halo readback when baking.
